text:
marta: Heads-up: I'm trying to run the JavaScript SDK inside a Bun edge worker for a demo and run the Deno test suite against the same package. Node installs fine, but Bun errors out with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` pointing at `./dist/index.cjs`. Anyone hit this import/export resolution mismatch?
kevin: Bun's resolver is picky about exports and prefers ESM. If package.json points `main` at CJS and `exports` favors node->cjs, Bun may pick a path it can't load. Try making an explicit ESM entry or a tiny ESM shim at the package root.
sam: Also check your `exports` map order. Bun sometimes follows the `default` field. If you only have a node CJS target, add a `default` pointing at your mjs build.
marta: Current package.json: `"main":"dist/index.cjs","exports":{ ".":{"node":"dist/index.cjs","default":"dist/index.mjs"}}`. Node resolves ok but Bun still throws.
jen: Aside from exports, runtime differences matter. We use webcrypto in auth; Bun and Deno expose different subtle APIs. That can break the auth initialization rather than imports.
kevin: Right — our auth does PBKDF2/importKey via `crypto.subtle`. Deno's webcrypto is standard, Bun had gaps historically. Add a runtime guard: `const subtle = globalThis.crypto?.subtle ?? (await import('node:crypto').then(c=>c.webcrypto.subtle))`. Keep it lazy so browsers/edges use their native impl.
sam: Fetch behavior is another frequent culprit. Bun's fetch lacks ReadableStream.getReader in some runtime builds; SDK code that calls `response.body.getReader()` will throw. Use feature-detect: `if (response.body && typeof response.body.getReader === 'function') ... else await response.arrayBuffer()`.
marta: My auth retry loop is failing in Bun: fetch throws inside our polyfill and the retry wrapper never triggers. Looks like the error shape is different. We should unify on throwing `FetchError` or check for `error.name` like `TypeError` and treat network errors consistently.
jen: For TypeScript consumers, Deno users reported `index.d.ts` referencing `node:` imports which Deno rejects. One fix: ship a deno-friendly d.ts or use conditional `types` exports in package.json pointing to a `dist/deno.d.ts`.
kevin: We could add an `exports` subpath: `"./deno": { "import": "dist/deno.mjs", "types": "dist/deno.d.ts" }`. Then Deno users can import `npm:@redwood/sdk/deno` or remap with import maps.
sam: Another approach: publish a tiny `platforms/` folder with `bun.mjs` and `deno.mjs` wrappers that re-export the ESM build but contain only runtime-safe shims (no node: imports). Consumers pick based on environment.
marta: For a quick unblock I patched node_modules with `deno.mjs` that re-exports `../dist/index.mjs` and edited the `.d.ts` to remove `node:` bare imports. It unblocked tests.
jen: Can we add a sample repo `examples/edge-bun-deno` showing recommended package.json (type:module, exports map with deno/bun entries), an import map for Deno, and a tiny polyfill script for Bun (crypto guard + fetch fallback)? That would be great for onboarding.
kevin: Also file a DX bug: detect `globalThis.Bun` on runtime and switch to a Bun-friendly codepath (avoid `node:` imports, relax getReader usage, crypto guards). Lowering the surprise for new users would cut support asks.
infra-bot: docs-builder: created `examples/edge-bun-deno` in the examples repo and added a small README and dev script.
marta: Awesome. I'll try that sample and paste my minimal repro here once I clean it up. If people want the quick patch I used, I can paste the snippet.
kevin: Please do small code snippets save hours. :thumbsup:
